Key Lessons from Failure Lab

  • More recurrent steps ≠ better reasoning. Saturation, oscillation, and noise amplification all cause diminishing or negative returns.
  • Latent reasoning is harder to debug. Without visible intermediate tokens, you must probe the hidden state to detect failure modes.
  • Memory is fragile. Recurrent memory can be overwritten by new demonstrations or corrupted by interference.
  • State capacity matters. Too small a state dimension creates a hard ceiling on representational capacity.
  • Decay rate is critical. Too high → saturation; too low → forgetting; just right → stable computation.
  • These are TOY MODEL failures. Real models (BDH, Coconut, Recurrent Depth) have more sophisticated dynamics but share these fundamental trade-offs.
REPORTED BY AUTHORS

Reported Failure Modes in Literature

BDH-CQ Limitations (Engdahl et al., 2026)
  • Ordering & nesting: fails to compose sequences
  • Conditional rule selection: cannot switch rules
  • Unseen parameter values: poor extrapolation
  • Composition: struggles with multi-step transforms
Coconut Limitations (Hao et al., 2024)
  • Training instability with multiple continuous thoughts
  • Larger models benefit less (language pre-training interference)
  • Requires careful multi-stage curriculum
  • Latent thoughts harder to interpret than CoT
Recurrent Depth Limitations (Geiping et al., 2025)
  • Not dominant paradigm yet
  • Oversight concerns vs verbalized CoT
  • Path independence needs more study
  • Convergence behavior not fully characterized
TRM Limitations (Jolicoeur-Martineau, 2025)
  • Optimal recursion depth exists (more → OOM)
  • Task-specific architectures needed
  • Why recursion helps so much = open question
  • EMA required for stability
